title: Ankylosaurus growl (sound design from real animal recordings)
author: DigiZoo sound design from recordings by National Park Service; NPS & MSU Acoustic Atlas / Jennifer Jerrett; Kent Wang
changes: Movie-style dinosaur call: no recordings of dinosaurs exist, so it was designed from real animal recordings (American alligator groan, grizzly bear roar and a hippopotamus snort, pitched down and layered). Sound design from 3 real recordings: "Alligator (NPS Sound Gallery)" 3.62–5.50 s, slowed to 0.7× speed (pitched down 30%); "Yellowstone sound library - Grizzly Bears Roar - 001" 1.00–3.40 s, slowed to 0.85× speed (pitched down 15%); "Hippopotamuses vocalising in South Africa" 0.05–0.27 s, slowed to 0.65× speed (pitched down 35%), placed at 0.10 s; then mixed to mono, gentle 12 dB/oct high-pass at 28 Hz, added reverb, silence trimmed, loudness-normalised (≈ −18 dBFS RMS, peak ≤ −1 dBFS), 10 ms fade-in / 120 ms fade-out, encoded as 96 kbps mono MP3.
